items.question: Digoxin inhibits which membrane enzyme?
items.explanation: Digoxin inhibits Na+/K+ ATPase, raising intracellular Na+ then Ca2+, increasing contractility.

items.question: Which drug is contraindicated with sildenafil due to severe hypotension?
items.explanation: Sildenafil (PDE5 inhibitor) with nitrates causes dangerous hypotension; the combination is contraindicated.

items.question: Ivabradine lowers heart rate by selectively inhibiting the ___ current in the SA node.
items.explanation: Ivabradine blocks the If current in the SA node, reducing heart rate without affecting contractility or BP.

items.question: Why does ivabradine cause visual phosphenes?
items.explanation: Ivabradine blocks retinal Ih channels (similar to cardiac If), causing transient luminous phenomena (phosphenes).

items.question: Why is the ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) not combined with an ACE inhibitor?
options: Increased angioedema risk from dual bradykinin accumulation
items.explanation: Both raise bradykinin; combining ARNI with an ACE inhibitor markedly increases angioedema risk (36-hour washout needed).

*PharmaCraft Daily - 30 Oct 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (CVS)
Q: Digoxin inhibits which membrane enzyme?
Ans: Na+/K+ ATPase
Why: Digoxin inhibits Na+/K+ ATPase, raising intracellular Na+ then Ca2+, increasing contractility.

🌍 *FMGE* (CVS)
Q: Which drug is contraindicated with sildenafil due to severe hypotension?
Ans: Nitrates
Why: Sildenafil (PDE5 inhibitor) with nitrates causes dangerous hypotension; the combination is contraindicated.

🩺 *NEET PG* (CVS)
Q: Ivabradine lowers heart rate by selectively inhibiting the ___ current in the SA node.
Ans: If (funny) current
Why: Ivabradine blocks the If current in the SA node, reducing heart rate without affecting contractility or BP.

🏥 *INI-CET* (CVS)
Q: Why does ivabradine cause visual phosphenes?
Ans: Retinal If-like channel (Ih) blockade
Why: Ivabradine blocks retinal Ih channels (similar to cardiac If), causing transient luminous phenomena (phosphenes).

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper III: Systemic)
Q: Why is the ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) not combined with an ACE inhibitor?
Ans: Increased angioedema risk from dual bradykinin accumulation
Why: Both raise bradykinin; combining ARNI with an ACE inhibitor markedly increases angioedema risk (36-hour washout needed).
